clue.text: Affectedly genteel inspector in foreign car

indicators.note: one thing sitting inside another means the first is placed within the second

blocks.note: the Lada is a Russian make of car
Detective Inspector, abbreviated

explanation.surface: A snooty police inspector driving around in an imported car.
explanation.walkthrough: The inspector goes inside the Russian car's name: LA-DI-DA.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes someone pretentious and posh in speech or manner, a close synonym.

clue.text: Recipe with good nosh concocted around yard for manager

indicators.note: something concocted is mixed up from its ingredients, so these letters get stirred into a new order
the mixed letters wrap themselves around the next item rather than sitting beside it

blocks.note: R is the doctor's abbreviation for recipe, a prescription
taken as written
taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: whip up good food around the yard for the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen words point to food, but the answer is a person: Roy Hodgson managed England's football team and several Premier League clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Roy Hodgson is a well-known football manager, so he is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Latin woman in trouble reared in Welsh place

indicators.note: the woman is placed in the trouble, so one item goes inside the other
in a down clue, rearing up means reading from the bottom upwards, turning the letters round

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for Latin
an ill is a misfortune or trouble
a woman's name

explanation.surface: A Latin woman in some difficulty, brought up in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: The woman goes inside the trouble before the reversal; in a down entry that reversal reads the letters bottom to top. Llanelli is a town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Llanelli is a town in south-west Wales, famous for rugby, so it is a Welsh place.

clue.text: Fierce look in old cricketer securing 50

indicators.note: securing something means holding it firmly within, so the number goes inside the name

blocks.note: David Gower, former England cricket captain
L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A retired batsman scowling as he reaches his half-century.
explanation.walkthrough: David Gower was an elegant England batsman of the 1980s; 50 is a half-century in cricket, apt for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to stare angrily, and as a noun a glower is an angry or fierce look.

clue.text: By the sound of it, painful area's to rise dramatically

indicators.note: the phrase asks us to go by what a word sounds like when spoken rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a sore is a painful spot on the body

explanation.surface: A sore spot that suddenly flares up and gets much worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices or birds that soar climb sharply and high, so the verb means to rise dramatically.

clue.text: Sports body holding quiet jolly in place of breeding?

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the sports body wraps the next item

blocks.note: FIFA is world football's governing body
sh is a call for quiet
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, RM

explanation.surface: A football organisation hosting a quiet party.
explanation.walkthrough: Jolly as a Royal Marine is a crossword favourite. The question mark flags that 'place of breeding' is a loose description.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm is a facility where fish are reared in tanks or pens, so it is somewhere animals are bred.

clue.text: Read about a Northern city beginning to waive church rules

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the reading word encloses what follows
the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: to con is to study or read carefully
taken as written
N abbreviates northern
LA, Los Angeles
the opening letter of waive

explanation.surface: Studying a northern city's records before setting aside the church's regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: CON wraps A and N to give CANON.
explanation.definitionFit: Canon law is the body of law made by a Christian church to govern its clergy and members.

clue.text: Hands are found on this fine brig at sea getting observational responsibility

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a cryptic description: a timepiece has hour and minute hands
these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors on a smart ship at sea taking on lookout duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' sounds like a ship's crew, matching the brig, but they are the hands of a clock face.
explanation.definitionFit: A watching brief is a lawyer's instruction to observe a case for an interested party, so it is a duty to keep an eye on things.

clue.text: Chance certainly to tuck into some meat

indicators.note: tucking something into another thing places it inside

blocks.note: loin is a cut of meat
OK as an agreeing reply, sure

explanation.surface: An opportunity, sure, to get stuck into a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tuck into' suggests eating, which fits the meat, but it is placing one piece inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-in is an informal word for an opportunity to take part or succeed.

clue.text: Playing area abandoned by college? That's nub of matter

indicators.note: when something is abandoned by a thing, that thing leaves, so it is dropped out

blocks.note: a sports field
C abbreviates college

explanation.surface: A sports field left behind by a university, which is the core of the issue.
explanation.definitionFit: The pith of something is its essential part or core, as in the pith of an argument.

clue.text: Signal shown in flat, perhaps, by mayor

blocks.note: a flat, such as B flat, is an example of a musical note
a mayor is an example of a local worthy, a dignitary

explanation.surface: A sign displayed in an apartment, perhaps by the town's mayor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Signal' reads as a noun, but it is the adjective, as in a signal achievement. Flat suggests a home; here it is music.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means striking or remarkable, so it is a synonym of noteworthy.

clue.text: Hooligan loitering initially behind museum

indicators.note: initially points at the start of a word, so only its first letter is taken

blocks.note: the V and A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London
the opening letter of loitering

explanation.surface: A yob hanging around at the back of a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' puts the L after the museum. The Victoria and Albert is a big London museum of art and design.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal deliberately damages property, a typical act of a hooligan, so the words are near synonyms.

clue.text: Female bully delivering a tirade (not half) about incomplete journey

indicators.note: not half means only part of the phrase survives, the back portion being lost
about here means surrounding, so the shortened tirade wraps the journey
incomplete means a word is left unfinished, so its tail is cut

blocks.note: to harangue is to lecture someone at length
a ride is a trip

explanation.surface: A domineering woman ranting half-heartedly about an unfinished trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivering a tirade' looks like the definition of a bully, but it is wordplay; only its first five letters survive, wrapped round a journey missing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a strict, bossy or belligerent old woman, which fits a female bully.

clue.text: Favoured still a US college from the south occupied by lecturer in a familiar way

indicators.note: in a down entry, starting from the south means reading from the bottom upwards
a place occupied by someone has that person inside it

blocks.note: being in means being in favour or fashion
yet as in nevertheless
taken as written
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
L abbreviates lecturer

explanation.surface: A popular academic still teaching at an American college, chatting on friendly terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole run 'still a US college' is reversed as one unit, and the lecturer's letter then slips in just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimately means in a close, personal manner, which is what acting in a familiar way implies.

clue.text: Fine vision I match when dolled up? Yes and no!

definitions.text: Fine vision I match when dolled up? Yes and no!

indicators.note: dolling up means dressing something in a new style, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: F abbreviates fine, as on pencil grades
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone checking the mirror, convinced they look perfect after dressing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is the speaker's own view: they think they look fine when dressed up, and onlookers would say yes and no.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashion victim follows trends slavishly, so believes they look great while others find the result ridiculous.

clue.text: Current requiring means for steering, we hear, in a set of boats

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken form, so the words are taken by their sound

blocks.note: a current is a flow of water
a tiller is the bar that turns a boat's rudder

explanation.surface: A water current needing something to steer a fleet of small craft.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, TILLER and the end of FLOTILLA sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats travelling together, so a group of vessels.

clue.text: Irish label in Ireland largely promoted water

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not fully, so the final letter is dropped
the label sits in the country name, so one goes inside the other
promoted means moved up, which in a down entry means reading the letters bottom to top

blocks.note: IR abbreviates Irish
Éire is the Irish name for Ireland
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: An Irish brand label raised in Ireland, used to market water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Water' looks like a noun, as bottled water, but it is the verb. Ireland's own name Éire is shortened before the label goes inside and the whole is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrigate is to supply land with water, so it works as the verb to water.

clue.text: My new canine is by part of cage in agricultural store

N abbreviates new
C stands for a canine tooth in dental notation
a rib is part of the ribcage

explanation.surface: A new dog of mine kept beside a cage on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: Cor is British slang for surprise. Canine suggests a dog, but here it is a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: A corncrib is a ventilated bin or building for storing and drying maize on a farm.

clue.text: List of duties for all to see obscuring small computing device

explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for a universal audience; it covers the S in ROSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A router is a networking device that forwards data between computers.

clue.text: Cold device used by couch potato?

second meaning: the handset for changing channels from the sofa

clue.text: Around home, get fun in altering late adjustments?

these letters to be rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Fine-tuning means making small final refinements, typically just before something is complete.

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

clue.text: Sun leaders in lurid excess always zealously expose such?

blocks.note: first letter of Sun
first letters of these five words

clue.text: A lucky charm man ignored in paper? He accepts whatever

taken as written

taken as written
